news.title: The Fed's main inflation measure will be released Wednesday. Here's what to expect
news.summary: Data is expected to show ongoing price pressures and consumers who nevertheless continue to spend.

news.title: Consumer optimism slides to lowest since 2014 as fears escalate over rising prices and jobs
news.summary: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index tumbled to 81.9, a decline of 6.7 points and a reading well below the forecast for 89.

news.title: America's Canadian import restrictions come into force. Here are the products barred from entry
news.summary: President Donald Trump says he expects Ottawa to concede to its demands on trade in the coming weeks, but Canadian officials insist they won't sign a bad deal.

news.title: Australia says more hikes not off the table after raising rates to 15-year high
news.summary: The hike of 25 basis points was in line with expectations by economists polled by Reuters.

news.title: China posts weakest industrial profit growth this year, expanding 4.2% in August
news.summary: Economists expect Beijing to lean harder on stimulus to stabilize corporate profitability, as consolidation accelerates in sectors facing sluggish demand and fierce competition.

news.title: Here's what happens to the economy when Treasury yields soar like they are now
news.summary: Government debt costs leaped higher Wednesday, the product of multiple factors.

news.title: Surging Treasury yields pose a brand new problem for Kevin Warsh and the Fed
news.summary: Markets expect the central bank will take a firmer hand on inflation. It's not that easy.

news.title: China saw 'surprise' jump in U.S. orders ahead of Trump-Xi summit, private survey shows
news.summary: A private survey shows a rebound in China's exports to the U.S. as companies position for continued stability between the world's two largest economies.

news.title: Switzerland is keeping rates at 0% — for now
news.summary: The Swiss National Bank held rates at 0% as low inflation and a strong franc enable it to diverge from other central banks, though markets expect hikes ahead.

news.title: Global debt tops $365 trillion as economists sound alarm over 'vicious cycle'
news.summary: More is being paid out by advanced economies in debt interest than the whole world spends on AI, defense or clean technology.

news.title: France's fresh budget battle threatens to topple another government
news.summary: Time is not on the side of French government bonds, strategists have warned, as the nation's deficit balloons.

news.title: World heads into food crises 'blind' as U.S. aid cuts squeeze UN food agency, experts warn
news.summary: Climate shocks, conflict and a global fuel crisis, on top of surging interest rates and donor cuts, leave agencies less able to help those facing higher food prices.

news.title: Why Japan’s markets flipped the usual script after central bank rate hike
news.summary: The yen weakened past 157 against the dollar, the yield on the 10-year Japanese Government Bond slipped, while the Nikkei 225 gained 1.5%.

news.title: France’s wine production nears a 70-year low, leaving winemakers with tough choices
news.summary: As the French wine industry reaches a crisis point, key players are considering new markets, products and generations.

news.title: Consumer sentiment is in the dumps despite a solid economy. Goldman Sachs blames 'lower happiness'
news.summary: Goldman economist Joseph Briggs said broader pessimism in society may be contributing to struggling consumer sentiment even as the economy chugs along.

news.title: Bank of England defies Fed’s rate-hike lead, leaving rates unchanged
news.summary: The Bank of England kept rates steady Thursday, even after U.K. inflation rose to 3.1% and energy costs put pressure on prices.

news.title: 'Science fiction': Transport companies — the backbone of economy — are sounding alarm on fuel prices
news.summary: Prices for diesel, the fuel type used to power trucks and trains, came in at an all-time high of $6.31 per gallon on Wednesday.

news.title: Consumers hit by one-two punch of oil and rates from Iran war. The estimated bill is $1,700 per household
news.summary: Rising oil prices and Treasury yields are lifting energy and borrowing costs for U.S. households, pushing consumers to draw more heavily on savings.
